main.title: The Game Awards
main.subtitle: A shared archive of the work we remember
main.summary: A celebration of game makers, with every category winner from 2014 onward.

cards.heading: What the awards celebrate
cards.text: The Game Awards celebrates the people who make games: designers, artists, writers, performers, composers and the teams around them. Created by Geoff Keighley in 2014, the annual show combines awards with performances, announcements and conversations about the medium.

cards.heading: A changing medium, a shared stage
cards.text: An awards archive is also a record of changing priorities. Categories make room for new ways to play and new kinds of work, from independent production and performance to accessibility and community support. Move through the years to read every category winner, then open the official ceremony beside the list.

main.title: The Last Guardian
main.subtitle: A boy learns to work with Trico
main.summary: The Last Guardian follows a boy and the enormous creature Trico, whose different abilities help them escape through a ruined complex.

cards.heading: A boy and an enormous companion
cards.text: The Last Guardian is Fumito Ueda, genDESIGN and Japan Studio?s 2016 PlayStation 4 adventure. A boy controlled by the player depends on the enormous creature Trico to travel through a ruined complex. Gestures, hesitation and cooperation shape their growing relationship.

cards.heading: Learning Trico?s responses
cards.text: Trico watches, becomes distracted and sometimes takes time to respond to the boy. Animation and AI let the creature react to nearby objects, surfaces and signals. Players learn to interpret its gaze, posture and movements while guiding it towards the next task.

cards.heading: Puzzles for different abilities
cards.text: The boy fits through narrow openings and reaches mechanisms; Trico can leap great distances and support the boy on its body. Puzzles combine these different abilities. Ueda recalled difficulties adapting some areas that had been built before Trico?s movement was fully defined.

cards.heading: From PlayStation 3 to PlayStation 4
cards.text: Announced for PlayStation 3 in 2009, the game returned publicly in 2015 as a PlayStation 4 project. Technical difficulties contributed to its lengthy development. Further bug fixing delayed the final release to December 2016, reaching North America on December 6 and much of Europe the following day.

main.title: Yakuza 6: The Song of Life
main.subtitle: Kiryu between two cities and a new family
main.summary: Yakuza 6: The Song of Life is a 2016 action-adventure game developed by Ryu Ga Gotoku Studio and published by Sega for PlayStation 4.

cards.heading: From the Japanese launch to Western editions
cards.text: Yakuza 6: The Song of Life is a 2016 action-adventure game developed by Ryu Ga Gotoku Studio and published by Sega for PlayStation 4. The English version was released in Southeast Asia in March 2018, and worldwide the following month. Versions for Windows and Xbox One were released in March 2021. The game was followed up by Yakuza Kiwami 2, a remake of the second game, and by Yakuza: Like a Dragon, the next chronological installment, released in 2020.

cards.heading: The Dragon Engine
cards.text: Kiryu explores the city before fights turn the same streets into improvised arenas. Yakuza 6 introduced the Dragon Engine, changing the presentation and the way bodies react during combat. Extreme Heat Mode makes Kiryu harder to knock back and turns finishing moves into more damaging actions while his Heat lasts. Progress uses several kinds of experience, each funding different improvements. Eating at restaurants provides some of that experience, but a hunger gauge limits repeated meals until time has passed. The system connects ordinary city visits to the abilities Kiryu will use in the next confrontation.

cards.heading: One fighter, two cities
cards.text: Unlike Yakuza 4, Yakuza 5 and Yakuza 0, Yakuza 6 does not feature any playable characters besides Kiryu himself. Additionally, unlike 0 and Yakuza Kiwami, Kiryu only uses one fighting style. This game features the series staple location of Kamurochō, Tokyo, as well as a new city, Onomichi, Hiroshima Prefecture. Onomichi stands out from other cities in the series in that its name is the same as its real world counterpart, with the area featured in game being a recreation of the city's Shingai district.

cards.heading: Kiryu and Haruka
cards.text: Yakuza 6: The Song of Life takes place in winter 2016, and features two major settings: the Kamurochō district of Tokyo, and the Jingaicho district of Onomichi, Hiroshima. Kazuma Kiryu (Takaya Kuroda) returns as the sole playable protagonist, along with several of his allies from previous titles in supporting capacities: Shun Akiyama (Koichi Yamadera), Makoto Date (Kazuhiro Yamaji), Daigo Dojima (Satoshi Tokushige), Goro Majima (Hidenari Ugaki), and Taiga Saejima (Rikiya Koyama). The story is centered around Kiryu's adoptive daughter, Haruka Sawamura (Rie Kugimiya), who has become a mother to an infant child named Haruto. Kiryu sets out to learn the truth about Haruto and the circumstances behind his birth, while being embroiled in a massive conflict between the Tojo Clan and several other crime organizations in Kamurochō and Onomichi.

main.title: Super Mario Run
main.subtitle: One finger is enough to get going
main.summary: Super Mario Run is a 2016 platform game developed and published by Nintendo for iOS and later Android.

cards.heading: Mario arrives on smartphones
cards.text: Super Mario Run is a 2016 platform game developed and published by Nintendo for iOS and later Android. It is Nintendo's first mobile game that is part of one of the company's long-running and major franchises.

cards.heading: Run automatically, jump at the right moment
cards.text: In Super Mario Run, the player controls Mario or other characters as they automatically run across the screen while timing jumps to collect coins and dodge enemies and hazards. As a Super Mario game, it contains a common plot wherein Mario must rescue Princess Peach, who has just been captured by Bowser. However, the player must also rebuild the Mushroom Kingdom destroyed by Bowser. The game had involvement of series creator Shigeru Miyamoto, and its development team consisted mostly of the original Super Mario development team, featuring many similar gameplay concepts adapted for ease of mobile controllers. The first four levels of Super Mario Run are free to play, but unlocking the rest of the game requires a one-time payment.

cards.heading: Replay value, price and connectivity
cards.text: Super Mario Run received overall positive reviews by critics. Reviewers generally praised the game's replay value and addictive gameplay, though common criticism was directed towards its comparatively high price in the mobile market, as well as its required connectivity to the internet. With 50 million downloads, it became the most downloaded mobile game in the first week. The total figure of downloads was 300 million as of September 2018.

main.title: Gravity Rush 2
main.subtitle: Find a new direction for down
main.summary: Gravity Rush 2 is Japan Studio's PlayStation 4 action-adventure, first released in Australia and Europe on 18 January 2017. Kat is drawn away from Hekseville and reaches another world, where the floating city of Jirga Para Lhao introduces new people and inequalities. Her ability to change gravity lets her fall toward a chosen direction rather than remain fixed to the ground. The sequel builds its exploration around that movement, filling the space above, below and between streets with routes that can be approached from several sides.

cards.heading: Find a new direction for down
cards.text: Gravity Rush 2 is Japan Studio's PlayStation 4 action-adventure, first released in Australia and Europe on 18 January 2017. Kat is drawn away from Hekseville and reaches another world, where the floating city of Jirga Para Lhao introduces new people and inequalities. Her ability to change gravity lets her fall toward a chosen direction rather than remain fixed to the ground. The sequel builds its exploration around that movement, filling the space above, below and between streets with routes that can be approached from several sides.

cards.heading: Change the weight of the same action
cards.text: Alongside Kat's familiar gravity style, Lunar makes her lighter and more agile, while Jupiter gives movement and attacks a heavier impact. Changing styles alters how a jump, approach or strike feels without changing the person being controlled. The player can match that weight to a particular threat or passage through the city. Gravity powers also allow nearby objects to become projectiles. A street therefore offers material for the next fight as well as a surface to leave behind when Kat chooses another direction to fall.

cards.heading: A city worth stopping inside
cards.text: Jirga Para Lhao's busy streets and distinct districts expand the social world around Kat, giving her people to meet and local tasks to complete between larger events. The scale of its floating architecture provides a practical reason to experiment with gravity, while the story follows the divisions within the city. Keiichiro Toyama returned as director, with Kohei Tanaka composing the music. The sequel developed the first game's central movement rather than replacing it, showing how the same power could support a broader world and more varied encounters.
